newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan awards huge oil concession to Canada's IPC.
newsitem.headline: Sudan awards huge oil concession to Canada's IPC.

text.p: Sudan has awarded the Canadian company International Petroleum Corporation (IPC) a concession to explore for oil in an area more than a third of the size of the country, the largest in Africa, state radio said on Thursday.
IPC president Ian Lundin signed the concession agreement in the capital Khartoum on Thursday with Energy and Mining Minister Awad Ahmed al-Jaz, the radio said.
It did not say where the 920,000 square km (355,000 square miles) concession was or give any other details.
Another Canadian company, Arakis Energy Corporation, holds a concession for Sudan's most promising fields, believed to hold up to 3.5 billion barrels.
Sources close to Arakis said last week that the U.S. company Occidental may be working with IPC on a concession close to the Arakis block.
Lundin said in Geneva on Friday that his company was also interested in plans to build a pipeline to the Red Sea from the oil fields in southern Sudan.
